representations.text:
Your March 30–April 12 records show a sustained change in movement despite stable steps: active time averaged 9 versus 54 minutes/day in your 28-day baseline, down 83%, while steps stayed near 8,000. Every day, including weekends, had only 8–12 active minutes, recorded at 21:00. Low movement rose from 450 to 602 minutes/day (+34%); individual bouts lengthened from roughly 44–47 to 59–61 minutes and extended until about 20:40–20:53. It eased slightly toward the end but never returned to baseline; low movement does not establish sitting.

Sleep remained near 7h51, with starts around 22:50 and waking at 07:00. Resting heart rate (~56 bpm) and RMSSD (~45 ms) also stayed stable. Activity versus following-night sleep showed only a weak relationship. No metrics were missing, and daytime wear stayed constant.

Your sleep changed for one week, then returned to your personal baseline. Sleep ending March 30–April 5 lasted 357–368 minutes, roughly two hours below your baseline average of 481 minutes. Starts shifted from about 22:39 to 00:32–00:43, while waking stayed at 07:00. From April 6–12, sleep returned to 474–485 minutes, averaging about 480, with starts at 22:35–22:46. This occurred across weekdays and weekends; the full-window average of 422 minutes hides that return.

Steps (~7,979/day), active time (54 versus 56 minutes, still at 21:00), low movement (~450 minutes), and resting heart rate (~56 bpm) stayed close to baseline. RMSSD averaged 44.2 versus 45.3 ms, remaining within your baseline range. Activity had only a weak relationship with following-night sleep, so it does not explain the sleep change. No metrics were missing.

Your March 30–April 12 pattern remained close to your 28-day baseline. Recorded sleep averaged 475 minutes in both periods, with an unchanged 01:00–09:00 schedule every day, including weekends. Nightly duration varied only from 472–479 minutes, without a sustained shift.

Steps averaged 7,935 versus 7,963/day; active time was 54 minutes in both periods, recorded at 21:00, and low movement averaged 449 versus 450 minutes. Steps and active time edged upward within the window, though their averages remained near baseline. Weekends retained somewhat higher steps than weekdays: 8,065 versus 7,883.

Resting heart rate was slightly lower (55.9 versus 56.2 bpm), and RMSSD slightly higher (45.8 versus 45.0 ms), both within your baseline ranges. Steps and active minutes barely correlated; activity versus following-night sleep showed only a modest negative association, without establishing causation. No metrics were missing.

Your main change was longer uninterrupted low-movement periods throughout March 30–April 12. Every day, including weekends, contained three bouts: 10:00–12:30, 12:45–15:25, and 15:40–18:30, lasting 150–170 minutes each. Your baseline instead had ten roughly 44–47-minute bouts separated by five-minute gaps. Total low movement increased more modestly, from 449 to 480 minutes/day (+7%), with no return during the window. These records do not establish sitting.

Active time stayed at 55 minutes/day, recorded at 21:00. Steps averaged 8,038 versus 8,026, although they trended downward within the window by about 29/day. Sleep remained near 7h51, starting around 22:49 and ending at 07:00, with little weekday/weekend difference. Resting heart rate (55.9 bpm) and RMSSD (45.6 versus 45.4 ms) stayed near baseline. Activity versus following-night sleep showed only a weak relationship. No metrics were missing.
